findings.evidence: The standalone “When a run, a review or an execution step calls an external AI CLI and acts on the result” section repeats the activation decision without adding runner-specific knowledge.
findings.fix: Record the removal of this body-only restatement; keep the trigger in frontmatter and the runner-specific decisions in the workflow.

findings.evidence: “Choose the runtime and model” starts a sound phased process, but the caller has no short checklist distinguishing what must be settled before launch, what proves completion, and what authorizes a follow-up.
findings.fix: Add a four-item caller checklist near the top: confirm owner-selected lane and role; resolve the runner and prepare capture; await the original launch and verify its result; take only the follow-up authorized by the exit and status. Link each item to its existing procedure.

findings.evidence: “Use when you run, wait for, read, retry or chain an external AI CLI” is specific, but the description omits the distinct herdr/headless intent covered by the body and the trigger set.
findings.fix: Use when asked to run an external review or execute a plan through ai-kit's cross-AI runner (cross-ai.mjs), wait for a lane, read AIKIT-XAI or per-setting results, continue a session, or stop a lane opening herdr tabs. Handles pi, OpenCode, Codex, Cursor, Copilot and Claude; passes role, model, effort, context, skills and MCP settings, and uses --argv-file for unsupported runtimes. Also use when a lane hits quota, 429 or a rate limit, exits 75 or 69, is locked or partial, or reports ignored settings, findings or retry_after_s. Interpret the result, apply the hard-tier wait or owner handoff, and answer GSD retry/skip/abort without switching harness, provider or model. Not for setting up reviewers or configuring GSD presets.

findings.evidence: “A hosted lane's run safety” puts the run-record schema, polling and truncation internals, sweep matching rules, and crash-remnant details inline. The 382-line body is about 7,200 words despite already having targeted references.
findings.fix: Keep the launch choice, the verdict signal, and the ambiguous-start and cleanup warnings inline. Move the full hosted safety and sweep detail to a hosted-troubleshooting section in references/launch-and-wait.md, linked from the host-failure and unconfirmed-close branches; a normal headless launch should not load that section.

findings.evidence: “running without a lock” is noted, but the caller still has to invent a concurrency policy when supervising a write-capable lane in an unwritable or full state home.
findings.fix: Make lock availability a precondition for launches that rely on checkout serialization. If the runner reports that it proceeded unlocked, do not start any overlapping lane; report the loss of serialization and require the owner to restore locking or provide an isolated checkout before further execute launches.

findings.evidence: The main launch case names plan-review.md and fake/ok but has “files”: []; the resume case supplies only prior stderr, not the next prompt or a fake CLI. The reset case also requires an exact wait without specifying a host or scheduler outcome.
findings.fix: Supply the named prompts and a hermetic fake-runtime setup for the launch and resume cases. Split the reset case into confirmed one-shot and no-scheduler handoff fixtures, asserting either a single eligible scheduled job or no job plus a complete handoff.

findings.evidence: “Arm a session wake so this run resumes after the usage limit” is labeled negative but does not identify what “this run” is; a cross-AI lane with retry_after_s would make it a positive.
findings.fix: Specify a native-session wake with no cross-AI runner in the negative, and add a paired positive using a runner-issued retry hint without naming the skill.

findings.evidence: “$ROLE is review for a review lane” omits a write before dispatch: the runner invokes migrateRetrySources for real calls regardless of role (cross-ai.mjs:7018), and that migration can rewrite the project's retry configuration and remove the legacy block (cross-ai.mjs:3631–3708). The quota reference describes migration, but the normal launch path says it need not be read.
findings.fix: Before launching a review that must not change files, check for pending legacy retry migration. If one is pending, stop for owner-approved migration in a separate step or use a prepared isolated checkout. Distinguish child review restrictions from runner-owned writes at the launch gate.

findings.evidence: “Both are already on disk” fails if prompt.md cannot be opened or the host kills the wrapper before it writes lane.rc; the workflow defines no safe outcome for a missing trailer or disagreement between the two exit codes.
findings.fix: Require both artifacts and matching exit codes before chaining or scheduling. If either is absent or they disagree, report an incomplete launch with the available shell or host evidence; verify whether the original process is still running and do not relaunch automatically.

findings.evidence: “It then resets the session session_resets times” omits the explicit-session branch. The runner pins an applied --session-id, sets sessionResets to zero for that run, and refuses fresh-session branches (cross-ai.mjs:5686–5690, 6053–6069).
findings.fix: Qualify the reset ladder: an explicitly applied --session-id pins the session and disables fresh resets. Point the resume workflow to that exception so the caller does not expect a new session after a pinned resume fails.

findings.evidence: “128+n | signal | the child died on signal n” attributes the status to the wrong process. The runner emits this status for a signal it catches (cross-ai.mjs:5388–5406); a child-only signal is logged as a child failure and goes through classification (cross-ai.mjs:6031–6045).
findings.fix: Describe 128+n as the runner's handled interruption, not proof of a child-only signal. For a child-only signal, report the final classified outcome and use the attempt diagnostic for the child signal.

findings.evidence: “opencode's help shows no notification or one-shot scheduling feature, so an opencode host uses the foreground wait” misses OpenCode's documented Shell background mode, which notifies the session at exit. This contradicts the reference's own capability-based branch.
findings.fix: Separate completion notification from delayed scheduling. When the current OpenCode Shell tool advertises background execution and completion notices, use that primitive for long launches; otherwise use foreground. Keep the delayed-retry handoff unless the current session actually exposes a verified one-shot scheduler.

findings.evidence: “gsd-core's 300 s default” is a version-sensitive upstream default without a dated official citation or an instruction to read it live. The runner separately has a 300 s built-in fallback.
findings.fix: Call 300 s the template's built-in fallback and tell callers to read the runner's effective deadline diagnostic. If retaining the claim about upstream GSD, cite the official source with the version and date checked.

findings.evidence: “When it cannot be confirmed, use the print-and-stop handoff” covers a missing or unclear scheduler response but not a job that was created without a usable confirmation. A manual retry could then overlap a scheduled one.
findings.fix: If creation is ambiguous, check the scheduled-task list for that lane. Confirm a single eligible job or cancel it and verify cancellation before giving the manual re-invoke handoff. If neither can be verified, report the uncertainty and instruct the owner not to re-invoke until the pending job is resolved.
